d: Stream instances within a player's camera view to support long-range gameplay scenarios such as scoped weapons and high-speed movement.
h:
Frustum streaming lets the server stream instances that fall within a player's camera view but lie beyond the normal streaming radius. It is an opt-in system that is additive to the existing streaming area and any active replication foci. It is not a replacement for standard instance streaming. Enabling frustum streaming provides new functionality for gameplay scenarios that require long-range visibility.

How frustum streaming works

In 3D graphics, a camera frustum is the pyramid-shaped region of the world visible on screen from the camera origin. Standard instance streaming replicates objects in a cube around the player's replication focus equally in all directions. When you enable frustum streaming for a player, the server also streams instances within a frustum shape matching the player's camera view, extending well beyond the normal streaming radius.

The total streaming area is a union of these shapes:

  • Primary streaming radius: the standard cube around the replication focus.
  • Frustum: the camera-view pyramid, active only when frustum streaming is on for that player.
  • Replication foci: any additional areas your scripts create with Player:AddReplicationFocus().

Frustum streaming does not remove or shrink the primary streaming area. Enabling it increases the number of instances that can be streamed to the client. This can increase both memory usage and potentially CPU usage. Normal instance and bandwidth quotas still apply.

Frustum streaming modes

The Player.FrustumStreaming property accepts one of four FrustumStreamingMode values:

  • Default: equivalent to Disabled. Lets scripts reset the property to its initial value.
  • Disabled: frustum streaming is off for this player.
  • Automatic: the engine activates frustum streaming when it detects qualifying conditions.
  • Enabled: frustum streaming is always active for this player.

In Automatic mode, the engine enables frustum streaming when it detects any of the following conditions:

  • Narrow field of view: the camera zooms in, such as when a player looks through a sniper scope.
  • High velocity while looking toward the direction of movement: the player moves quickly in a consistent direction, such as in a racing experience.
  • Camera distance from the replication focus: the camera moves far from the player's replication focus, such as in a free-camera mode.

Automatic mode introduces a short activation delay after it detects a qualifying condition. If you need finer control, consider manual control (Enabled), where you can activate frustum streaming manually. For example, you could activate frustum streaming during an equip animation to have a scope ready by the time the player looks through it.

Enable frustum streaming

Frustum streaming is controlled per player through the Player.FrustumStreaming property. This property can only be set on the server. If client-side logic needs to trigger a mode change, fire a RemoteEvent to a server Script that validates the request and sets the property.

Use automatic mode

Set the property to Automatic for each player when they join. The engine handles activation and deactivation based on camera and movement conditions.

Enable Automatic Frustum Streaming

local Players = game:GetService("Players")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.FrustumStreaming = Enum.FrustumStreamingMode.Automatic
end)

Control frustum streaming manually

Toggle frustum streaming from a server Script based on your own gameplay logic. The following example enables frustum streaming when a player equips a scoped weapon and returns to the default behavior when they unequip it.

Toggle Frustum Streaming on Scope Equip

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local scopeEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ScopeEvent")

scopeEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, shouldFrustumStream)
    if shouldFrustumStream then
        player.FrustumStreaming = Enum.FrustumStreamingMode.Enabled
    else
        player.FrustumStreaming = Enum.FrustumStreamingMode.Default
    end
end)

Because the property is server-only, the client fires a RemoteEvent to request the change. Always validate the request in the server script before setting the property.

Stream-out behavior

Frustum streaming works with both StreamOutBehavior settings:

  • Opportunistic: instances that leave the camera view and fall outside the normal streaming radius or any active replication focus linger for 1.5 seconds and then are garbage collected.
  • LowMemory: instances that leave the camera view remain streamed indefinitely. The engine only removes them once the client's memory runs low, and only if they are outside the camera view at that point.

In both modes, instances inside the primary streaming radius or an active replication focus remain streamed regardless of whether they are in the camera view.

Performance and device behavior

Frustum streaming increases the number of instances present on the client. This increases memory usage and can increase CPU usage. The server gives the frustum the same budget for instance count and bandwidth as a replication focus. Roblox might adjust this allocation in the future if games commonly use both frustum streaming and replication foci and the frustum needs higher priority.

The frustum streams outward to the lesser of the client's current draw distance and an engine-defined maximum range. If the client reduces graphics quality or experiences low frame rates, the engine reduces draw distance. When draw distance falls to or below the normal streaming target radius, the engine disables frustum streaming for that client automatically.

Limitations

  • Server-only property: Player.FrustumStreaming has no effect when set from a client script. Use a RemoteEvent to relay client input to the server.
  • Fast camera movement: when the player rotates or moves the camera quickly, the engine invalidates the current frustum and begins streaming again from the center outward. During rapid rotation, the effective frustum narrows to a beam centered on the camera direction. Instances at extreme range might churn in and out of the streamed set.
  • No occlusion culling: the frustum shape does not account for walls, terrain, or other geometry blocking the player's actual view. All instances within the frustum volume are candidates for streaming.
  • Draw-distance dependency: frustum streaming requires a draw distance greater than the normal streaming target radius. On devices with reduced graphics quality or low frame rates, the engine might disable frustum streaming automatically.
  • Additive cost: frustum streaming adds instances and full quality terrain to the client and increases resource usage. It does not reduce the streaming workload.
  • Not applicable to non-streaming experiences: if your experience does not use instance streaming, all instances are already present on the client and frustum streaming has no effect.

kid.simple: With streaming, a player normally only gets the world loaded in a box around their character. That is a problem if they look through a sniper scope or race at high speed, because faraway things they should see are not loaded. Frustum streaming fixes this by also loading what is inside the player's camera view, even far away. You turn it on per player from a server script, and it costs extra memory, so use it when your game needs long-range viewing.
kid.analogy: Normal streaming is like a lantern that lights a circle around you. Frustum streaming adds a flashlight beam pointing where you are looking, so you can see far ahead in that one direction.
keyPoints: Frustum streaming adds to normal streaming. It never shrinks the normal area around the player.
The total loaded area is the normal box around the player, plus the camera-view shape, plus any extra replication foci.
Set `Player.FrustumStreaming` to Default, Disabled, Automatic, or Enabled. Default works the same as Disabled.
Automatic turns on by itself when the camera zooms in (like a scope), when the player moves fast toward where they are looking, or when the camera is far from the player. It has a short delay.
Enabled is always on. Use it to switch on early, like during a scope-equip animation, so the view is ready.
The property only works when set by the server. A client must ask the server with a RemoteEvent, and the server should check the request.
With Opportunistic stream-out, things that leave the view (and are outside the normal area) are removed after 1.5 seconds. With LowMemory they stay until memory runs low.
It does not see walls, so things behind a hill can still load. On low graphics settings, the engine may switch it off automatically.

terms.frustum: The shape of what a camera can see: a pyramid with its tip at the camera, getting wider the farther it goes.
terms.streaming radius: How far around the player the world is normally loaded. By default, the target is 1024 studs.
terms.replication focus: A center point the world is loaded around. Normally your character.
terms.additive: Added on top. Frustum streaming loads extra, it does not replace anything.
terms.field of view: How wide the camera sees. A sniper scope has a narrow field of view, like 10 degrees instead of the normal 70.
terms.velocity: Speed in a direction, like 100 studs per second forward.
terms.draw distance: How far away the device is willing to draw things. Lower graphics settings shrink it.
terms.garbage collected: Removed from memory because it is no longer needed.
terms.occlusion culling: Skipping things hidden behind walls. Frustum streaming does not do this, so hidden things can still load.
terms.churn: Things loading and unloading over and over, which can happen when the camera spins quickly.
terms.validate: Check that a request makes sense before doing it, so cheaters cannot abuse it.

example.title: Turn on frustum streaming only while a sniper is equipped
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (a LocalScript in the tool fires the ScopeEvent RemoteEvent with true or false)
example.code:
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

-- Create the RemoteEvent the client will fire
local scopeEvent = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
scopeEvent.Name = "ScopeEvent"
scopeEvent.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

scopeEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, wantsScope)
	-- Validate: the value must be true or false
	if typeof(wantsScope) ~= "boolean" then
		return
	end

	if wantsScope then
		-- Validate: the player must actually be holding the sniper
		local character = player.Character
		if not (character and character:FindFirstChild("Sniper")) then
			return
		end
		player.FrustumStreaming = Enum.FrustumStreamingMode.Enabled
	else
		player.FrustumStreaming = Enum.FrustumStreamingMode.Default
	end
end)
explain: Only the server can set `FrustumStreaming`, so the client sends a message with a RemoteEvent.
First we check the message is really true or false, because a cheater could send anything.
When a tool is equipped, it moves into the character, so we check the character has a tool named Sniper.
If everything checks out we set Enabled, so far targets in the player's view load in. When they put it away, we set it back to Default.

watchOut: Setting `player.FrustumStreaming` in a LocalScript. It does nothing there. Set it on the server.
Turning it on for everyone all the time in a game that does not need long-range views. It uses more memory and can slow down phones.
Trusting the client's request without checks. Always validate before changing the setting.
Expecting it to work in a game without StreamingEnabled. Everything is already loaded there, so it has no effect.
